Archer Aviation has agreed to acquire former rival Wisk Aero from Boeing, along with SkyGrid and Insitu Inc, in a deal that will give Boeing about a 16.5% stake in Archer after closing. The acquisition follows a 2021 trade-secret lawsuit between Archer and Wisk that was settled in 2023 and led to a collaboration on autonomous technology; Archer has also raised $430 million for its defense business and another $300 million from institutional investors including BlackRock and Wellington in 2025.

14,567 followers [...] Archer Aviation has reached a definitive agreement to acquire three Boeing subsidiaries — Wisk Aero, Insitu, and SkyGrid — in an all-stock transaction announced on August 10, 2026. The deal moves Archer from a pre-revenue eVTOL developer into a diversified aerospace and defense contractor. Boeing will receive an equity stake in Archer, invest up to $55 million in an upcoming funding round, and receive up to $200 million in warrants to purchase Archer stock, making Boeing the largest outside shareholder in Archer. [...] Three years after settling a trade secret lawsuit, electric aircraft company Archer Aviation now owns its former rival, Wisk Aero.
Under the terms of the deal, Boeing has agreed to sell Wisk Aero and two other subsidiaries to Archer in exchange for an ownership stake in the company, according to a regulatory filing released Monday. The other subsidiaries are SkyGrid, a digital airspace and air traffic management software company, and drone maker Insitu Inc.
Boeing will receive newly issued Archer shares equal to 19.75% of Archer’s shares outstanding immediately before closing, resulting in about a 16.5% stake in the company after the deal, according to a regulatory filing and a person familiar with the matter.

The Boeing Company (NYSE: BA) and Archer Aviation Inc. (NYSE: ACHR) today announced the companies have signed definitive agreements in which Archer will acquire Boeing’s Wisk Aero, SkyGrid and Insitu subsidiaries. The deal will combine complementary capabilities developed over decades in autonomy, electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft, and unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) – creating a groundbreaking end-to-end physical AI platform for aerospace and defense. [...] Archer’s Founder and CEO, Adam Goldstein said, “This is a watershed moment for Archer and the future of physical AI in aerospace and defense. This is the next big step forward in becoming a diversified platform, rapidly growing our revenue base and bringing scale to our business.”

In conjunction with the transaction, Boeing and Archer are entering into a collaboration and technology-sharing arrangement through which Boeing will retain access to the Wisk core autonomous flight technology for its current and next-generation commercial and defense aircraft. The transaction allows Boeing to retain strategic upside through its stake in Archer and simultaneously focus current and future investments into Boeing’s core businesses. [...] “This transaction is a win-win for Boeing and Archer,” said Brian Yutko, Boeing vice president, Commercial Airplanes Product Development. “It allows Wisk, SkyGrid and Insitu to accelerate capability development and time to market while ensuring Boeing capitalizes on its investments in these technologies over the past two decades through continued development in our core businesses. Having worked with the incredible teams in these companies firsthand, it’s clear this transaction will create an industry leader in the advanced aviation market. We look forward to collaborating with Archer to drive continued innovation in aerospace, defense and autonomy.”

### Archer to Shape Physical AI Future of Aerospace and Defense with Acquisition of Boeing’s Wisk Aero, Insitu and SkyGrid Subsidiaries; Boeing to Invest in Archer and Collaborate

ARLINGTON, Va. & SILICON VALLEY, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- 
The Boeing Company (NYSE: BA) and Archer Aviation Inc. (NYSE: ACHR) today announced the companies have signed definitive agreements in which Archer will acquire Boeing’s Wisk Aero, SkyGrid and Insitu subsidiaries. The deal will combine complementary capabilities developed over decades in autonomy, electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft, and unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) – creating a groundbreaking end-to-end physical AI platform for aerospace and defense. [...] Archer’s Founder and CEO, Adam Goldstein said, “This is a watershed moment for Archer and the future of physical AI in aerospace and defense. This is the next big step forward in becoming a diversified platform, rapidly growing our revenue base and bringing scale to our business.”

In conjunction with the transaction, Boeing and Archer are entering into a collaboration and technology-sharing arrangement through which Boeing will retain access to the Wisk core autonomous flight technology for its current and next-generation commercial and defense aircraft. The transaction allows Boeing to retain strategic upside through its stake in Archer and simultaneously focus current and future investments into Boeing’s core businesses. [...] “This transaction is a win-win for Boeing and Archer,” said Brian Yutko, Boeing vice president, Commercial Airplanes Product Development. “It allows Wisk, SkyGrid and Insitu to accelerate capability development and time to market while ensuring Boeing capitalizes on its investments in these technologies over the past two decades through continued development in our core businesses. Having worked with the incredible teams in these companies firsthand, it’s clear this transaction will create an industry leader in the advanced aviation market. We look forward to collaborating with Archer to drive continued innovation in aerospace, defense and autonomy.”

.png.small.400x400.png)Archer Aviation and Boeing announced today that they have signed definitive agreements for the former to acquire the latter’s Wisk Aero, SkyGrid, and Insitu subsidiaries. Boeing will also take a stake in Archer and enter into a collaboration and technology-sharing arrangement with the company. [...] Archer said the acquisition combines complementary capabilities in autonomy, eVTOL, and UAS developed over decades by the three subsidiaries, which they say will create a “groundbreaking” end-to-end physical AI platform for aerospace and defense. The company said the deal adds a defense business generating more than $200 million in annual revenue, based on Insitu's current financials and estimates, with operations across 35 countries.

Wisk has designed, built and flown six generations of eVTOL aircraft over 16 years, amassing more than 1,700 flight tests, the companies said. SkyGrid has developed a ground-based, aircraft-agnostic air traffic management platform intended to support automated airspace integration. [...] "This is a watershed moment for Archer and the future of physical AI in aerospace and defense," said Adam Goldstein, Archer's founder and CEO, in the release. "This is the next big step forward in becoming a diversified platform, rapidly growing our revenue base and bringing scale to our business."

Under the collaboration arrangement, Boeing will retain access to Wisk's core autonomous flight technology for use in its current and future commercial and defense aircraft.

# Archer Aviation to Acquire Boeing Subsidiaries Wisk Aero, Insitu, and SkyGrid

-  by Richard Pettibone

Archer’s Midnight eVTOL. Image – Archer Aviation

Archer Aviation and Boeing have reached a definitive agreement for Archer to acquire three of Boeing’s subsidiaries: Wisk Aero, SkyGrid, and Insitu. The deal transfers key autonomous flight, air traffic management, and uncrewed aircraft operations to Archer while granting Boeing an equity stake in the urban air mobility developer. [...] Under the terms of the transaction, Boeing will receive newly issued Archer Class A shares and warrants, ultimately positioning the aerospace giant to hold a stake of nearly 20 percent in Archer. In addition, Boeing has agreed to invest up to $55 million in an upcoming Archer funding round and will retain rights via cross-licensing to access Wisk’s core autonomous flight systems for its own commercial and defense platforms.

The acquisition brings three specialized defense and autonomous tech units under Archer’s management: [...] Archer plans to integrate the software architectures and flight histories of the three companies into its proprietary artificial intelligence foundation platform, ZEE. Combined, the acquired units account for nearly two million total flight hours.

As part of the broader strategic agreement, Boeing will retain access to core autonomy technologies for application in its main product lines, while Archer assumes operational control over the development of autonomous air taxis and tactical platforms. The transaction remains subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals.

Today, we signed definitive agreements to acquire @Wisk.aero, @Skygridai, and @Insitu\_inc from @Boeing, with Boeing taking a stake in Archer and becoming a strategic partner. We anticipate closing the transaction by year end.   
  
Wisk will accelerate our Halo/Thunder dual-use aircraft platform. Deploying nascent tech early in defense benefits our entire business.
